summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 45% YoY to INR3,132 crores and PAT 79% to INR762 crores, with EBITDA margin near 35%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR1,576 crores, up 39% YoY, with EBITDA of INR557 crores (about 35.3% margin) and PAT of INR382 crores (about 24% margin), broadly flat sequentially. Finance cost fell to about INR9.5 crores from INR55.2 crores a year earlier after IPO-funded debt repayment. Cell output reached 513 MW at 89% effective utilisation, while module output was 952 MW at about 44% utilisation. Order book stood at about 10.4 GW after record inflows of about 1.5 GW in the quarter, and the 6 GW integrated cell and module expansion remains on schedule (module by December 2026, cell by March 2027).

segments.name: Solar modules
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 production was 952 MW, up about 40% YoY from 682 MW, with module utilisation at about 44%; management sees a sustainable range of 45% to 60%.

segments.name: Solar cells (TOPCon)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 production was 513 MW, up about 61% YoY from 319 MW, at 89% effective utilisation; G12R cell manufacturing started in the last quarter. Cells are also sold to other manufacturers, with merchant volume broadly flat to marginally higher QoQ.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,200 to 2,400 crores; management said the H1 run-rate (INR1,100 crores per half) means the upper end is achievable.
FY27 EBITDA guidance of about INR2,400 crores reaffirmed; management described it as comfortably reachable given H1 performance.
Cell utilisation expected near 90% for the remaining two quarters of FY27.
6 GW integrated TOPCon expansion: module line by December 2026, cell line by March 2027; equipment shipping from end-October with arrival by November.
Post-expansion installed capacity to rise to about 16.3 GW modules and 8.9 GW cells, designed for broadly equivalent annual output.
Capex of about INR5,500 crores for the 6 GW project, of which hard cost is about INR4,600 crores and about INR700 crores is IDC and working capital margin money.
State capital subsidy (25% on the earlier project) and similar incentives expected on upcoming projects; treated as upside and not modelled in guidance.
Backward integration into ingot and wafer (9 GW, two phases of 5 GW and 4 GW) is planned, timing dependent on ALMM List-III and market conditions.
capex_capacity: 6 GW integrated cell and module project: equipment ordered, FAT under way, shipments from end-October 2026, module line ready by December 2026, cell line by March 2027.
Post-expansion capacity: about 16.3 GW modules and 8.9 GW cells.
Interest during construction is being capitalised until commissioning; a portion is expected to hit P&L from March 2027 quarter and fully from Q1 FY28.
Over 50% of cell capacity has been converted to G12R; remaining M10R lines to be converted after current orders are completed.
Company has no mono PERC capacity; all capacity is TOPCon for the last two years.
demand_pricing: Order book about 10.4 GW as of 30 September 2026; Q2 inflows about 1.5 GW, the highest in a single quarter; about 5 to 5.5 GW expected to deliver in the next 12 to 15 months.
Order book mix: about 70% DCR and about 30% non-DCR.
Q2 inflows: about 40% to 45% open access (C&I and IPP); IPP inflows carry delivery timelines within 12 months.
Module sales split: about 25% retail and KUSUM, about 75% institutional (C&I and utility).
DCR accounted for more than 50% of sales in the quarter, and management expects that to continue.
Management cites India installations of about 27 GW (AC) in the first half of calendar 2026, equivalent to about 35 GW DC, with domestic module demand tracking about 64% YoY growth.
Management said non-DCR margins are broadly unchanged, citing product, quality and track-record differentiation.
Silver use cut to about 60 to 65 mg per cell from about 220 mg earlier; G12R cells reach about 9.5 W against 8 W in the older single-cell format.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 6 GW capex (about INR5,500 crores, roughly INR9 billion per GW) well above industry cell-plus-module cost estimates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR5,500 crores covers both cell and module; hard cost is about INR4,600 crores, with the rest IDC, contingency and working capital margin money (about INR700 crores). Management also cited design, automation and lower silver use as reasons.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold if module prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices may fall somewhat, but margins can be maintained through silver reduction (220 mg to 60-65 mg), the move to G12R and manufacturing efficiency, with savings passed on to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did creditor days fall from 64 in FY26 to 25 in H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is a dynamic outcome of vendor negotiations; lower credit days were accepted in exchange for better prices, which helps COGS.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the largest customer's revenue share rise to 44% in Q2 from 19% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue share shifts quarter to quarter with delivery timelines; sales are backed by substantial advances or LCs, so credit risk is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin moderate QoQ even as DCR mix rose to about 54%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing depends on operational efficiency, raw material cost and module efficiency, and that EBITDA per watt is the metric it tracks.

qa_highlights.question: Does the ALMM-II deadline of December 2026 risk further deferral?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said deferral looks extremely unlikely; utility projects bid before August 2025 still need ALMM-II compliance, and about 30% of the order book is non-DCR.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a reduction in other expenses that is one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited open-access renewable power (100% of Q2 power), AGVs in cell lines, and a forex gain, and said similar expense levels should continue until the expansion starts.

risks_watch: ALMM-II (cell) implementation from December 2026 and the DCR timeline; C&I deliveries may slip past December commissioning.
Module utilisation is only 44%, while cell utilisation is 89%; ramp-up of the 6 GW module capacity needs to match cell output.
Industry cell capacity growth and possible module price declines; management says margins can hold, but gross margin moderated QoQ in Q2.
Finance cost to rise from the March 2027 quarter as interest capitalisation ends; INR828 crores drawn in the quarter for the expansion.
Largest customer concentration (44% of Q2 revenue) and its credit profile.
Incremental order inflows needed to fill the expanded 16.3 GW module capacity; the company says the current order book covers the upcoming capacity.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and margins, with clear timelines for the expansion. Less specific on module utilisation targets, the split of cell merchant sales, the DCR versus non-DCR revenue split, and the reasons for the largest customer's revenue share jump, which were deflected.
key_quotes: Our performance has remained consistent with the guidance we provided, even as the industry transitioned through changes in the implementation of ALMM regulations and geopolitical issues.
So, our order book is at a very healthy level that is required for the next financial year.
So, it looks right now extremely unlikely. And I was addressing your point on the capacity that is required for the implementation.
We have no mono PERC, sir. We have everything TOPCon from the last 2-years.
